title: Multi-site treatment investigation with column-selective missingness screening, post-treatment exclusion, interaction gate and site-specific vs pooled contrasts
source_relation: adapted: end-to-end statistical investigation and interaction-aware report audit expressed as a coupled multi-step function contract
difficulty_hypothesis: Agents call na.omit() across the whole table (dropping valid rows with missing post_adherence), include the post-treatment variable post_adherence as a covariate, fit separate per-site regressions instead of extracting site contrasts from the joint interaction model, report a pooled main effect even when treatment-by-site interaction is significant, or reverse the active-minus-control contrast sign.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The workflow relies on base R linear-model projection, contrast extraction and statistical study-design hygiene rather than external package APIs or version-sensitive functions. It serves as a multi-step statistical workflow control for measuring tool-use overhead on complex reasoning tasks.
mcp_relevance.information_need: How to extract within-site treatment contrasts and standard errors from a joint interaction model and how to gate pooled main effects on the interaction F test.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes: base R stats::lm, vcov, model.matrix and anova are standard and locally documented
alternative_solution_paths: lm(outcome ~ baseline + site / arm - 1) or cell-indicator parameterization for direct within-site contrasts
lm(outcome ~ baseline + site * arm) with linear combinations over coef() and vcov()
explicit QR / normal-equation OLS projection in base R

calibration_risks.ceiling: low-moderate: multiple coupled statistical and data-hygiene steps

pinned_evidence.oracle: explicit normal-equation OLS projection ((X'X)^-1 X'y) and contrast variance c'(X'X)^-1 c * sigma^2 in plain matrix arithmetic; cross-checked at load against stats::lm and stats::anova
